A dashcam or two at the windscreen and rear window? Might drain the battery a bit. There are types that have accelerometers that will continually loop and then record X number of seconds if there is a collision/acceleration. A good 1080P camera might record many details even down to the license plate as the car gets close. I don't know how these work unattended though (if more than one collision occurs while unattended, so the recording restarts and saves).

As for an exterior camera, there are many different manufacturers of DVR type camera systems. For high detail you would need at least a 1080P camera or even a 4K camera.

Camera types come in various lens settings - from 2.8mm to 25mm. This setting determines the field of view of the lens and magnification details. A 2.8mm camera will record details to about 2m with a 60deg or so field of view. A 25mm camera will record out to about 20m with a field of view of maybe 25deg. You give up field of view for detail.

Check Amazon first for some DVR systems that meet your needs - probably a good 1080P system with hard drive storage capability. Then search for that system.

Personally, I don't like the wifi capable systems, because the signal can be interrupted, or just slow. But hard wiring external cameras is also a pain in many ways as well.

If you are electronically minded, a Raspberry Pi with a camera that takes pictures front and back when an accelerometer triggers might be handy. The Pi could also be set up with an alarm so you could hear when the collision occurs, and ring the police. Raspberry Pi sends pics over wifi to phone or computer and you can provide the plate number while the offender is still driving.

Annke has an event record option that is pretty easy to set up and marks the recording every time something happens. It can be set for motion detect in the field of view, or with an actual 'line crossing' type sensing.

I had a spare drive, and have it on 8 day loops, with up to 8 cameras on a 2TB drive.
